evidence: Numerical-uncalibrated simulation (sim/js/concepts/kite2, results.json) on the shared re-audit rules; closed-form polar estimates anchored to cited full-size canopy data. Nothing built, measured or validated. Polar, reefed glide, boom pointing, heave compensation, governor and docking are ASSUMED until bench/tow tests.

name.en: K2-R3 reefing drogue kite cam on an actively pointed boom (heave-compensating, KE-governed winch)
name.zh: K2-R3 收口圆伞风筝相机：主动指向臂杆 + 升沉补偿/动能调速绞盘

oneLiner: A ≈90 g slotted round canopy (documented L/D 0.75, half of it kept when reefed) on a 7 m line from the tip of a 1.2 m telescopic boom that a stabilised 2-axis gimbal points at the kite camera; a pack winch heave-compensates the body motion, goes to a soft clutch above the KE governor speed and reels in fast on braking so the kite docks on the boom axis before the rider stops.

rootCause.ke: Iteration 2 (re-run): every ensemble KE peak sat at the first hockey stop (t≈37.9 s). The body lean flips from ≈+48° to −40° in ≈0.4 s, so the exit (mast tip) moves 8–9 m/s relative to the rider CoM and yanks the 86 g kite through the elastic line to 17–18.5 m/s ground speed while the rider is at 11–13 m/s. With L/D 0.75 a second source appears: in crosswinds the kite is blown to 45–67° azimuth and carving swings it at 6–9 m/s laterally. Ground-frame KE of the kite at rider speed (13.2 m/s max in the ensemble) is only 7.6–9 J; the excess was all relative motion created by the device.
rootCause.footage: Any rigid exit (mast or boom) seen from a camera at the line end projects onto the rider: a passive line-aligned boom lags the line by ≈1.4° and shows as a 10–20 px stub (art >3 % in ≈45–55 % of frames). Iteration 2 never counted its 0.35 m mast as artefact. Only active pointing at the camera (end-on, ≤3 px) keeps the artefact below 3 %.
rootCause.headClear: A line from the pack top passes 0.4–0.5 m from the helmet centre; ≥1 m needs the exit ≥≈0.65 m from the pack along the line, i.e. a boom.
rootCause.clothesline: In hard carving the whole body inclines ≈45°: the pack top is ≈1.0–1.1 m above the snow and the line/boom rises at the station elevation (≈30–35° with the honest polar). No exit position on the body puts the line ≥2 m above the snow 1 m behind the rider in carving.

changes: Polar defaults: gMaxR 0.75 (MC-1-1C), reefed-glide retention 0.5 (reefGloss 0.5); flying mass 78 g ×1.15 = 89.7 g incl. the 3 g slot/reef/douse hardware (A2-X-09).
Heave-compensating winch: feed-forward of the exit velocity relative to the rider CoM along the line (pack IMU + boom encoders), base command slew-limited 20 m/s², fast reel-in 7 m/s on braking.

KE governor: kite ground speed > √(2·12.5 J/m) (from the actual mass) → clutch 2 N; reel-in limited to the largest r with |v_rider + r·ê| ≤ vGov − 0.3; fast-dock when the rider is within 1 m/s of vMaxFilm = min(vKE(14.9 J) − 2, vGov − 0.5).

Exit: 1.2 m 5-section telescopic carbon boom (0.26 m collapsed) on a stabilised 2-axis gimbal (rear cone ±110° az, −35…+80° el), pointed at the kite camera; tip trumpet (45° residual) + snuffer sleeve; boom out only when flying (1.5 W).

Launch: boom extends with the canopy still in its sleeve; tip pitot must confirm ≥1.6·vMin + 1 m/s; canopy released reefed (steady opening pull ≤4 N), filling distance 6·D0, opening-shock factor 1.8, streamer drag 20 %; climbs on a short line before paying out; elevation target capped at what the polar can reach; reef opened (8→14 N) when the kite is low or off azimuth.
Glide direction of the round canopy stored as a physical vector (the angle-in-a-frame form flipped on the wind axis — a singularity also present in iteration 2).
No re-inflation on snow: a landed canopy is reeled in and docked (or hand-stowed after a simulated walk if it lies outside the rear cone); body force = raw 50 ms mean at the integration step.
Head safety: overfly (kite leaves the rear cone) → flag + soft pay-out, retrieve when back behind; short line and kite within 1.3 m of the helmet or >10° out of the cone → snap onto the tip.
Wind gates on windEstimate(); airspeed in flight from the KCU pitot; azimuth authority scaled with the 2 s-mean airspeed (full ±45° side shots only at ≥12 m/s).
Proximity radar (4 m, 0.2 s) → clutch soft and climb; boom contact modelled (backdrivable gimbal, 10 N magnetic breakaway, impulse reported).
Shot plan: ±15° rear-quarter station, side swap, two commanded 8 s side shots to ±45° (azimuth span).

lines: ASSUMED (4–5 g digital micro servo class); shared 2.5 g servo is too weak for 20–40 % of a 6–25 N line load (audit K2-02)
KCU shell, 0.2 m carbon camera arm, funnel seat cone
8 suspension lines 0.7 m, reefing line + rings, slot/flag lines
slot frames, reefing rings, dousing line, hi-vis flag hardware

name.en: K2-R reefing drogue kite cam (steerable lifting drogue)
name.zh: K2-R 收口圆伞风筝相机（可操控升力拖伞）

iteration2.oneLiner: An 86 g kite whose lifting surface is a 0.40 m² slotted ROUND canopy: vent-slot opening sets L/D 0–1 (statically stable, MC-1-1C/MC-6 principle) and therefore the ≈43° rear-quarter elevation, continuous skirt reefing (drag area 1→0.25) plus a gust-absorbing winch set the 6–20 N pull, and a 0.35 m folding exit mast raises the line and carries the line-aligned dock trumpet.
whyRedesign: Audit K2-01 is confirmed by the literature: a soft wing reaches L/D ≤1 only in its post-stall band where CR ≈0.9–1.25 (TN D-4182, TN D-4672) and where it has no static trim (TN D-4672: none between α 30° and 75°; TN D-4182: violent oscillations above 50°). AoA depower gives CR 0.2 only at L/D ≈3 (TU Delft kites) → zenith, top-down. The iteration-1 corner (CR 0.2 at L/D 0.5–0.7) does not exist.

Elevation needs L/D 0.5–0.9 (tether ≈30–42° from the up-slope apparent wind → 43–55° above horizontal); pull must stay ≤40 N from 4 to 25 m/s apparent wind (q ratio ≈40). With CR fixed near 0.9 by the low L/D, only AREA can vary the pull → reefing.

A slotted round canopy is the only soft lifting surface with a documented, statically STABLE glide of L/D 0.75–1.2 (MC-1-1C, MC-6) and it can glide in any direction about its axis (yaw), and round-canopy skirt reefing has quantified drag-area data (Knacke/Ares: 0.25 at reefing ratio 0.2).

optionsQuantified.option: Keep the soft wing, honest polar, active pitch stabilisation (design 4)
optionsQuantified.numbers: ensemble avail 65.05 %, KE max 22.36 J, ops max 3; collapses on the α 22.5°/75° boundaries in nominal (4); plus undemonstrated pitch stabilisation

optionsQuantified.option: Smaller canopy / no reefing at honest CR (design 3)
optionsQuantified.numbers: pull ∝ V²: nominal mean 29.0 N, 18 m/s body force 102 N; ensemble avail 61.9 %, body force max 181.98 N. Shrinking the area to keep ≤40 N at 25 m/s raises v_min above ≈6 m/s (closed form) so tailwinds/pushes are lost
tether trails at the slope angle (≈15° above horizontal) minus sag → line and kite at head height or on the snow
adopted partly: view elevation ensemble mean 42.63° (p90 44.91°); concept gate relaxed 50→55°; moguls 57° fails
only for transients: pay-out above max(14 N, 1.35×2 s mean); steady high-q pull cannot be absorbed by line length (would run out 7 m in <1 s at 21 m/s)

optionsQuantified.option: Second line/anchor pulling the kite down-and-back
optionsQuantified.numbers: two lines from the same rider do not change the aero equilibrium; a snow anchor/drag body puts a line on the snow behind the rider
L/D 0.6 needs CL≈0.04 at CD0≈0.06: L/D swings 0→2 per few degrees, frame mass ≥15–25 g more, rigid spar in a 2 L pod and higher KE

chosenArchitecture.kite: 0.40 m² nominal (≈0.71 m) slotted round canopy, Skytex 27, 8 suspension lines 0.7 m, two rear vent-slot gores, skirt reefing line through rings; KCU pod with 3 × 4 g servo-winches (slot opening, reefing, differential slots = yaw), 4K camera on 0.2 m arm, 1.2 Wh cell
chosenArchitecture.polar: CD0 0.80 on nominal area, L/D = 1.0·u (u = slot opening), CD −12 % at full opening, glide loss 30 % at full reef (ASSUMED); stable at every u

lines: ASSUMED (4–5 g digital micro servo class); shared 2.5 g servo is too weak for 20–40 % of a 6–25 N line load (audit K2-02)
KCU shell, 0.2 m carbon camera arm, funnel seat cone
8 suspension lines 0.7 m, reefing line + rings, slot/flag lines

chosenArchitecture.pod: 2.3 L pod: BLDC winch, 30 N slip clutch, 1.5 N free-spool on line-contact detection, 12 Wh pack (80 g), heated dock holster (0.6 W, counted), 0.35 m folding mast tilted 15° back with a gimballed trumpet (accepts ≤120° off the mast axis)
chosenArchitecture.control: window-frame station loop (az ±15°, 28° above slope); outward channel → slot opening on the polar; tangential → yaw of the glide force (any direction below the wind axis); pull → reefing; winch: length hold + gust pay-out; retrieve: 3.5 m/s in calm, 1.5 m/s in wind; dock planner: funnel cone and ≥0.25 m helmet clearance, ≤3 retries, else safe flag-and-land (+1 action, +15 s)
chosenArchitecture.interlocks: launch only if armed AND descending (>0.3 m/s) AND on-snow vibration signature (ASSUMED sensor) AND rider 3.5–13.6 m/s; any 3 m climb auto-disarms; dock above 14.6 m/s rider speed (KE)

iteration2.note: iteration-2 design notes (superseded); its ensemble/sensitivity numbers were on the old judging basis

killTests: Tow/car-top test of the 0.40 m² slotted round + KCU at 6–15 m/s: L/D vs slot opening unreefed (kill if <0.6: avail 73.02 % at 0.6) and at reef 0.25/0.35/0.5 (kill if retention <0.3 or coning >10°).

Heave-compensation winch bench: replay the measured hockey-stop exit motion (8–9 m/s, 0.4 s) on a moving anchor with a 90 g dummy: kill if the dummy ground speed exceeds √(2·14.9 J/m) or the winch lag >30 ms.
Governor: 2 N soft clutch at 7 m line; drogue deceleration on the soft line within 0.3 s.
Boom: 1.2 m telescopic on a 2-axis gimbal pointing at a moving target with ≤0.5° error at 20 Hz under carving vibration, 0.13 N·m gravity load; real footage artefact <3 % of subject height.
Dock: 500 seats onto the boom-tip trumpet at ≤45° residual (wet/iced, 0–9 m/s); snuff + retract ≤2.5 s.
Reefed launch from the boom tip at 7–14 m/s: success ≥98 %, 50 ms pull ≤20 N, never within 1.3 m of the helmet.
Clothesline / bystander: written resort permission; boom breakaway and crossing-skier tests (impulse ≤2 N·s).
Optic: ≤20 g 4K M12 module with 55–65° HFOV.

envelope.credible: Rider 7–16 m/s, apparent wind ≥7 m/s to launch and ≥4.2 m/s to keep flying; wind 0–9 m/s head/cross and calm (avail 85–90 %), tailwinds degrade (tail-3 ≈80 %, tail-6 ≈55–80 %, tail-9 ≈20–40 %); low-traffic pistes with written permission only (line/boom 0.8–1.3 m above the snow 1 m behind a carving rider); stow while standing only facing the wind.
envelope.requires: L/D ≥≈0.7 unreefed for avail ≥80 % (KE/force/head clearance hold down to 0.6); flying mass ≤≈100 g for avail; active boom pointing ≤≈0.5°; heave-compensating winch ≥7 m/s with ≤30 ms lag.

round4.evidence: numerical, uncalibrated simulation on the shared round-4 rules (48 cases FULLRUN_CASES_R4, bodyPx ≥300, artefactCounts ≥2 px, helmetAt headClear, realistic actuators/estimators); not physical verification; G-MATURE closed

name.en: K2-R4 reefing drogue kite cam: passive hair-thin boom + motorised fishing-reel winch
name.zh: K2-R4 收口圆伞风筝相机：被动细臂杆 + 电动渔线轮式绞盘

firstPrinciples: A boom from the pack is ALWAYS projected onto the rider from a kite-borne camera (the line goes from the camera to the pack). The only way it stops being an artefact under the ≥2 px rule is to be thinner than ≈5 mm at ≈350 px/m. A boom aligned with the line by a free pivot is a two-force member in TENSION, so it can be a 3.0→2.5 mm carbon tube (inertial bending ≤0.008 N·m, ≤4 MPa in the ensemble spot runs).
A free pivot needs no gimbal motor: the audit3 torque deficit (0.35–1 N·m demand vs 0.13 N·m motors) disappears; 108 g and 1.5 W saved.

Pay-out (gusts, body heave yanking the exit) is the dangerous direction and needs no motor: a friction drag on an anti-reverse spool slips instantly above its setting (fishing-reel principle). The motor only reels in, inside a real Kv/R/current/voltage/inertia envelope, and holding costs zero current.

Height of the line 1–3 m behind the rider is set by the kite elevation (≤ atan(L/D)≈37° above the slope for the documented drogue, less when reefed) and the pack height in carving lean; raising it structurally needs a rigid member resisting T·Δh ≈8–14 N·m, which is ≥10 mm thick and therefore an artefact. So the clothesline gate cannot be met by this architecture; mitigation is force/impulse limitation, not clearance.

changes.boom: passive 6-section 3.0→2.5 mm carbon telescopic tube, 1.45 m (was 1.2 m, 12→4 mm, actively gimballed); free damped pivot τ=2/√(3T/mℓ); 2.5 mm tip ring; docking cone moved onto the KCU; canopy snuffed by fully cinching the reefing line (no tip sleeve); 5 N magnetic breakaway; 40 g (was 148 g)
changes.winch: motorised reel: 2205-class 2300 KV motor (Kt 4.15 mN·m/A, 0.08 Ω, 25 A, 10.8 V), 5:1 planetary, 12 mm spool → no-load 6.24 m/s, 36.8 N stall, reflected inertia 0.44 kg; anti-reverse bearing; servo friction drag (τ 0.08 s, 120 N/s, static/dynamic 1.15) holding max(14 N, 1.35×mean); solenoid release to 2 N (τ 0.02 s); reel-in feed-forward only as slack take-up, 0.6 m/s dead band; 85 g
changes.governor: drag release on the ESTIMATED kite ground speed (noise 0.2 m/s, 50 ms lag); threshold 11 J (was 12.5 J)
changes.sensing: pitot/vane apparent wind coloured noise 0.4 m/s (τ 0.3 s) in the window controller, reef feed-forward, low-airspeed logic and the launch tip-pitot check; heave estimate 0.3 m/s + 40 ms lag
changes.camera: 45° HFOV 4K (was 60°), boresight tilted 2.5° down, reframing on the whole-subject bounding box, crop sized on a ±0.6 s running max (body ≈60 % of height, subject ≤78 %); filming line 5 m (was 7 m)
changes.headClear: judged against helmetAt(raw shared run); boom length 1.45 m is what keeps the line tip ≥1 m from the helmet in carving lean (1.2 m → 0.84 m)

clothesline.metric: height above the snow of the boom + line 1, 2 and 3 m (horizontal) behind the boom pivot, every airborne riding sample; lowShare = % of those samples with the lowest of the three below 1.8 m
clothesline.target: ≥1.8 m everywhere 1–3 m behind (adult neck/face height, ASSUMED gate from the brief)
clothesline.verdict: FAIL: the line/boom is below 1.8 m within 3 m behind the rider for most of the filming time; no exit geometry can hold a ≥1.8 m line near the rider without a rigid member that resists T·Δh (8–14 N·m) and is then ≥2 px wide in the shot

crossingSkier.scenario: neighbour crosses 0.35 m behind at 8 m/s (cross: helmet top 1.9 m; crosspole: pole raised to 2.3 m)
crossingSkier.mechanism: rear radar (4 m, 0.2 s) drops the reel drag to 1.5 N and the kite climbs; a line contact is detected in 60 ms and the solenoid holds free-spool; the 25 g boom is on a free pivot with a 5 N magnetic breakaway (effective struck mass ≤25 g)

reefKeep_0.3.label: 30 % of the glide kept at full reef

IDEALISED_sensors.label: IDEALISED (not judged): noise-free sensing, no estimator lag

motor_weak_15A_9V6.label: reel motor 15 A limit and 9.6 V sag

no_governor.label: ablation: KE governor (solenoid drag release) off

killTests: 3 mm telescopic boom: 500 extend/retract cycles wet/iced at −15 °C, joint play, survival of a 30 N side load and a fall onto it; ≤2 px visibility in real 4K footage at 5–9 m
Reel drag: holding force repeatability ±10 % over temperature, stick-slip ratio (sens 1.3 → KE 14.85 J), solenoid release time ≤20 ms
KE margin is 0.6 J at nominal: LD 0.6 → 17.3 J, mass +15 % → 16.95 J, governor off → 16.05 J, noise-free sensing 15.4 J — measure kite ground speed in hockey stops before anything else
Round canopy L/D 0.75 and reefed glide retention at 0.7 m diameter (avail 67.6–73.9 % over the bracket)
Clothesline: crossing-skier contact on a dummy (line ≤10 N, boom impulse ≤0.2 N·s) and written resort permission

envelope.def: rider 7–16 m/s, apparent wind ≥7 m/s to launch; head/cross/calm 0–9 m/s avail 77.7–90.2 %; tailwind ≥3 m/s degrades (3–5.5 m/s 57–69 %, 6 m/s 44.5 %, 9 m/s 24 %); empty/low-traffic pistes only (clothesline)

round4.verdict: 12/13 shared metrics pass on the 48 cases with realistic actuators; avail FAILS (72.30 %, p10 54.74) because of the tailwind band; clothesline gate FAILS (line/boom 0.74–0.84 m above snow at worst, below 1.8 m in ≈90 % of filming samples within 3 m behind).
